papers.title: A novel function of neuroligin 3: Beyond sociality, Regulating lifespan in Drosophila
papers.abstract: Neuroligins are conserved postsynaptic adhesion proteins involved in synaptic function and behaviour. In Drosophila melanogaster, Neuroligin 3 (Nlg3) regulates social behaviour, sleep and synaptic architecture. We now report, through analysis of publicly available transcriptomics data, confirmed with RT-qPCR data, that loss-of-function of the nlg3 gene downregulates the expression of longevity-associated genes foxo, hsp70s, and hsp68. Graded genetic manipulation of the Drosophila melanogaster neuroligin 3 (nlg3) gene indeed modulates both social spacing and lifespan. Specifically, reduced nlg3 expression (via heterozygous deletion, or transposable-element insertion) extends lifespan in both sexes, while overexpression or complete deletion shortens it. In contrast, overexpression or complete loss of nlg3 leads the flies to be further apart (increased social distance, or social space), as does RNAi knockdown, while heterozygous reduction of nlg3 expression either lowers or does not alter the flies social space. This work identifies a previously unrecognized link between a conserved synaptic gene, social behaviour, and organismal longevity.

papers.title: High-resolution temporal profiling reveals synchronized dynamics of the mouse gut microbiome
papers.abstract: Background The gut microbiome undergoes diurnal oscillations entrained by host circadian rhythms and feeding behavior, and disruption of these oscillations has been linked to metabolic dysfunction. However, the temporal organization of microbial activity within these oscillatory cycles remains poorly understood, largely because conventional sampling approaches lack the temporal resolution needed to resolve rapid microbial dynamics. Results To address this gap, we developed a fully automated fecal collection system that enables continuous sampling from individual mice at minute- to hour-scale resolution without manual intervention. Using this platform, we collected fecal samples at hourly intervals over 14 consecutive days from individually housed mice. To reconstruct genome- and function-level trajectories from these data, we developed a cost-effective method (GORIN) that combines full-length 16S rRNA gene amplicon sequencing with long-read metagenomic references. Applying a newly developed phase-analytic method (NPPD) to determine the instantaneous phase of each genome and functional gene, we found that the gut microbiota is organized into two phase-coherent groups corresponding to the light and dark phases of the host circadian cycle. These two groups differed in gene content, suggesting distinct carbohydrate utilization strategies, with the light-phase community enriched in mucosal glycan-degrading enzymes, whereas the dark-phase community was enriched in carbon storage metabolism and motility-related functions. Within each phase, microbial taxa and functional genes displayed reproducible temporal succession across individual mice. Perturbations, including cage transfer and antibiotic treatment transiently disrupted phase synchronization, as measured by the phase order parameter, followed by gradual recovery of phase coherence. Conclusions These findings reveal reproducible phase-synchronized temporal organization in the mouse gut microbiome, with community-level phase relationships that can be quantified and tracked over time and following perturbation. The automated sampling platform, genome-resolved profiling framework, and phase-analytic metrics introduced here provide a scalable strategy for characterizing community-level temporal dynamics in host-associated microbial ecosystems, with potential applications for understanding how disruption of microbial temporal organization contributes to dysbiosis.

papers.title: mTOR signalling, not clock gene rhythms, organises daily physiology
papers.abstract: Daily rhythms in mammalian physiology are widely attributed to rhythmic transcription of "clock-controlled genes" driven by the circadian transcriptional/translational feedback loop (TTFL). Here we show that daily physiology can be uncoupled from the TTFL: inhibiting the mechanistic target of rapamycin (mTOR) abolishes most daily variation in cellular and organismal physiology, whilst clock protein rhythms persist. In cultured cells and mouse liver, functional rhythms are lost, including the proteome, RNA abundance, substrate utilisation and drug metabolism. In forebrain, most daily variation in protein abundance and phosphorylation is lost, yet locomotor activity and sleep-wake architecture are largely preserved in mice and zebrafish. PERIOD2 binds mTORC1 and limits its activity, providing a route by which clock proteins shape daily mTOR signalling. mTOR inhibition preferentially suppresses output over clock gene rhythms in Arabidopsis and Neurospora. We conclude that mTOR is a conserved conduit through which circadian and environmental timing impose daily organisation on physiology.

papers.title: Single-nucleus transcriptomics links telencephalic cell signatures to ocean acidification effects on social behaviour in a coral reef fish
papers.abstract: Mutualistic interactions are fundamental to the health and stability of reef ecosystems. While elevated CO2 has been implicated in impairments in interaction behaviours, how this environmental change alters cellular states and intercellular communication in the brain remains unresolved. Here, by analysing the single-nucleus RNA profile of ~66,000 telencephalic nuclei from a keystone mutualist, the cleaner wrasse (Labroides dimidiatus), interacting under ambient or elevated CO2 conditions, we identify highly cell type specific neural responses to elevated CO2. We highlight a substantial depletion in Oligodendrocyte Precursor Cells (OPCs), notably linked to oligodendrocyte myelination and neural structure maintenance. Elevated CO2 also elicited targeted transcriptional shifts across discrete cell types, characterised by widespread glutamatergic signalling and altered co-expression networks associated with pH regulation, energetic metabolism, and circadian rhythm, thereby compromising the cleaner's physiologic equilibrium. Additionally, cell-cell communication was altered under elevated CO2, including remodelling in SEMA4 and PTPR signalling pathways within radial glial and OPCs, respectively, revealing network signalling rewiring in response to the changed environment. These findings uncover the high-resolution neural substrates vulnerable to ocean acidification, providing mechanistic insight into how climate-driven environmental changes alter brain function and destabilise complex mutualistic ecological interactions.

papers.title: Theta-Phase Targeted Encoding Gates Memory Sensitivity
papers.abstract: Theta phase has been proposed to play an important role in memory. It may gate encoding and retrieval, such that certain phases are more favorable for memory processing than others, or become part of the memory representation, such that reinstating the encoding phase benefits retrieval. To test and distinguish these competing accounts, we used a closed-loop EEG system, allowing us to control the phase at which items were presented at encoding and retrieval. In an associative memory task, visual targets were presented at predefined phases of the ongoing mid-frontal theta rhythm, thereby pairing individual memory items with specific encoding phases. During retrieval, targets appeared either at the same phase as during encoding or at an alternative phase. We show that theta phase during encoding predicted subsequent memory sensitivity, while finding no evidence that retrieval phase nor the match between encoding and retrieval phases influenced performance. Therefore, our findings are consistent with a gating account, in which the rhythmic state at the moment of encoding influences the efficacy of memory formation.

papers.title: EEG decodability of facial expressions and their stereoscopic depth cues in immersive virtual reality
papers.abstract: Face perception typically occurs in three-dimensional space, where stereoscopic depth cues enrich the perception of facial features. Yet, most neurophysiological research on face processing relies on two-dimensional displays, potentially overlooking the role of stereoscopic depth information. Here, we combine immersive virtual reality (VR), electroencephalography (EEG), and eye tracking to examine the neural representation of faces under controlled manipulations of stereoscopic depth. Thirty-four participants viewed computer-generated faces with neutral, happy, angry, and surprised expressions in frontal view under monoscopic and stereoscopic viewing conditions. Using time-resolved multivariate decoding, we show that EEG signals in immersive VR conditions can reliably differentiate facial expressions. Stereoscopic depth cues elicited a distinct and decodable neural signature, confirming the sensitivity of our approach to depth-related processing. Yet, expression decoding remained robust across depth conditions, indicating that under controlled frontal viewing, the neural representation of behaviorally distinguishable facial expressions is invariant to binocular depth cues. Eye tracking showed that expression-related gaze patterns contained comparable information but did not account for neural representations, while depth information was absent in gaze patterns--consistent with dissociable representational processes. Our findings demonstrate the feasibility of EEG-based neural decoding in fully immersive VR as a tool for investigating face perception in naturalistic settings and provide new evidence for the stability of expression representations across depth variations in three-dimensional viewing conditions.

papers.title: Interactions of Sleep and Repetitive Behavior in Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Autism, and Intellectual Disability
papers.abstract: Objective: Sleep problems and restricted and repetitive behaviors (RRBs) feature in neurodevelopmental conditions such as autism, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and intellectual disabilities (ID). It is unclear whether their interaction differs between conditions, and whether symptom dimensions might capture differences better than diagnostic categories. Method: In a preregistered cross-sectional analysis of the Healthy Brain Network community sample enriched for neurodevelopmental conditions (n = 2,394, 5-21 years), linear regression modeled parent-reported sleep disturbance and RRBs by diagnostic category and symptom dimensions (autistic traits, ADHD traits, IQ). Results: All symptom dimensions predicted sleep disturbance (p < .001), whereas only ADHD consistently predicted greater sleep disturbance (d = .35, 95% CI [.24, .47]) among diagnostic categories relative to typical development. All diagnostic categories and symptom dimensions were associated with RRB severity. Sleep disturbance and RRBs were associated in the entire sample (beta = .30, p < .001). Sleep disturbance predicted RRBs at all levels of autistic and ADHD traits, but most strongly with high autistic and low ADHD traits (beta = .16) and least strongly when both were high (beta = .13). Dimensional measures explained more variance than diagnoses for sleep disturbance (R square = .14 vs .03) and RRBs (R square = .38 vs .21), and provided better model fits in all comparisons. Conclusion: Autistic and ADHD traits shaped the relationship between sleep disturbance and RRBs, whereas diagnoses did not. Neurodevelopmental symptom assessments might be more informative than diagnoses to manage sleep and RRBs, though the cross-sectional design and parent report limit inference.

papers.title: Neural mechanisms by which spaced learning promotes understanding
papers.abstract: Human learning must build understanding that can be reconstructed and extended, especially as artificial intelligence advances. Spacing improves retention, with neural mechanisms studied for memory; a few studies show benefits for understanding, yet none has examined its neural basis. Here, learners inferred unfamiliar word meanings from familiar component words, reconstructing an intrinsic explanatory relation. Schedules were equated at a criterion-verified immediate endpoint before delayed EEG retrieval. Spaced learners revised written explanations more often, in smaller steps converging on shared formulations, and later reported greater explanatory retrieval fluency than massed learners. Spacing showed greater differentiation from once-learning than massing over right frontocentral and temporal sensors (520-740 ms); a right-temporal subset was indirectly associated with the fluency advantage. A visual word-recognition model matched early-stage activity only under once-learning and massing, but word identity under all schedules. Earlier encoding-stage similarity and retrieval-stage differentiation may be successive windows on the reorganisation making understanding reconstructable.

papers.title: Mental replay rescales the subjective duration of past events via alpha and theta oscillations
papers.abstract: Human memory recall is flexible in time, allowing past events to be mentally replayed at variable speeds. However, it remains unclear whether temporally rescaled replay distorts the perceived duration of remembered events, and whether such distortion is tied to changes in the retrieved content. Here we instructed participants to mentally replay previously encoded naturalistic videos at compressed, expanded, or self-paced (free) speeds while recording scalp electroencephalography (EEG). Replaying an event at an expanded pace lengthened participants' subsequent judgments of its original duration relative to free and compressed replay, and the longer an event had been replayed, the longer it was judged to have lasted. Crucially, recalled memory content was unaffected, with gist accuracy and recalled detail comparable across speed conditions. During replay, alpha and theta power were reduced under compression, and both interacted with the speed instruction in predicting reported duration. Specifically, alpha power exhibited a stronger positive relationship with duration judgments under compressed replay than under free or expanded replay. Conversely, the relationship between theta power and reported duration was significantly more positive under expanded replay than under free or compressed replay. Neural pattern similarity between instructed and later spontaneous replay varied with replay speed, yet this reinstatement neither predicted reported duration nor mediated the oscillatory effects. These findings suggest that remembered duration is not read out from the amount of content retrieved but reconstructed at retrieval through oscillatory dynamics, decoupling the subjective scaling of time from the content of memory.

papers.title: Bridging Sensory Extraction and Decision Dynamics: Face Pareidolia Emergent from Bottom-Up and Top-Down Interactions
papers.abstract: Face pareidolia-the illusory perception of faces in everyday objects-provides a unique window into how the human brain resolves visual ambiguity. Whether pareidolia arises from bottom-up sensory processing or top-down, expectation-driven feedback, is currently debated. Here we recorded electroencephalography (EEG) while participants viewed rapid serial visual presentation (RSVP) streams of images, each of which was an object-to-face morph generated along a 21-image continuum via text-to-image diffusion models. Time-resolved representational similarity analyses revealed a clear spatiotemporal dissociation, in which early occipitotemporal areas tracked physical feature changes linearly, while later frontocentral channels collapsed this structural gradient into a sharp, sigmoidal profile reflecting discrete categorical decisions (face-like versus object-like). To characterise information transmission between these regions, we implemented a novel transformation-based representational connectivity analysis. These analyses uncovered an initial feedforward flow of information that transferred and transformed posterior linear traces into anterior sigmoidal representations. Crucially, partitioning the image continuum revealed that unambiguous stimuli (faces or objects) were predominantly resolved via feedforward information flow, whereas ambiguous pareidolic images recruited prolonged top-down feedback. Furthermore, perceptual decision sensitivity was biased by animacy priors and directly predicted individual behavioural reaction times during the task. Together, the findings help reconcile prior debate by establishing that face pareidolia is neither a feedforward process nor an isolated top-down projection, but an active, multi-stage recurrent process driven by feedforward feature extraction and top-down categorical resolution.

papers.title: Defining cell type-specific diurnal gene expression in the mouse retina
papers.abstract: The mammalian retina exhibits daily oscillations in gene expression that contribute to retinal physiology and visual function. However, the extent to which these temporal patterns differ among retinal cell types remains incompletely understood. We performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing in the mouse retina over the day and night, identifying rhythmic genes in the six major retinal cell types. Distinct diurnal gene expression patterns across photoreceptors, interneurons, retinal ganglion cells, and Muller glia correspond to their diverse functions across the light cycle. Even core circadian clock genes exhibited differences in paralog expression and rhythmicity across the retina. In contrast, dopamine signaling via the DRD4 receptor is highly rhythmic across most retinal cell types, suggesting dopamine signaling may be a key rhythmicity cue in the retina under diurnal conditions. This dataset highlights the complexity of daily transcriptional regulation in the retina and provides a resource to explore cell-type-specific diurnal rhythms.

papers.title: Capturing the rhythm: methodological choices shape inference from circadian activity data
papers.abstract: Abstract 1. Statistical tools and analytical decisions for analysing animal activity data are often limited and poorly justified, particularly with respect to model choice, sampling design and temporal aggregation. These shortcomings can constrain our ability to draw accurate and biologically meaningful inferences about behaviour. 2. We interrogated 24 h activity data taken from individual males and females derived from five Drosophila melanogaster populations to generate a general framework for collecting and analysing activity data that systematically compares common model classes, continuous verses fragmented sampling strategies, and alternative temporal aggregation choices (time-bin sizes). 3. Our analyses identified generalised additive mixed models (GAMMs) applied to high-frequency continuous data with small-moderate bin sizes (1-5 minutes) as providing the most robust and interpretable inference for our complex, high-frequency activity data. 4. However, our interrogation of the data set confirmed that analytical and sampling decisions need to be tailored to the study species, the timing of activities and the nature of the behaviour of interest. Accordingly, polynomial and cosinor generalised linear models, increased but biologically targeted snapshot sampling, and bin sizes smaller than one hour yielded adequate analyses with similar biological conclusions when appropriately matched to the system. 5. Our approach provides an accessible decision-making framework for activity analyses that allows researchers across behavioural, ecological and evolutionary studies to justify and optimise choices about data collection and modelling. Such an approach improves the biological relevance of inference and supporting the use of modern tracking and analytical technologies.

papers.title: Neural and Gait Adaptations to Dual-Task Demands in Children and Young Adults: A Mobile Brain-Body Imaging (MoBI) Study.
papers.abstract: Cognitive-motor interactions describe the complex interplay underlying how the brain manages concurrent demands on motor and cognitive processing. Yet, how cognitive-motor interactions present across childhood and young adulthood remains understudied, particularly through multi-modal methods which include neurophysiology. We investigated development of cognitive-motor interactions using a dual-task study design including simultaneous motor (walking) and cognitive (visual Go-NoGo) tasks. Using mobile brain-body imaging, (MoBI), we recorded simultaneous EEG, gait kinematics, and task performance. 61 neurotypical 8-to-30-year-olds completed the Go-NoGo while seated or walking on a treadmill. With increased age, participants became faster and more accurate on the task, walking became less variable, and N200 and P300 ERP amplitudes increased. Two distinct effects of cognitive-motor interactions emerged with age. An N200 amplitude attenuation when walking became exaggerated with age, suggesting older participants engaged greater neurophysiological flexibility to support their improved task performances, whereas children performed less well and may not have needed to recruit the same adaptive neural mechanisms. Additionally, an attenuation of stride variability during dual-task walking lessened with age, demonstrating robust motor development under dual-task conditions. These findings demonstrate a distinct pattern of changes to cognitive-motor interactions through development. Future research can examine how this pattern varies in different developmental conditions.

papers.title: Identification of PUFA interaction site on ASIC3 suggests a complex regulatory mechanism
papers.abstract: Inflammatory mediators including polyunsaturated fatty acids (PUFAs) potentiate ASIC3 by altering channel gating, yet the molecular basis for their interactions remains poorly defined. Using all-atom MD simulations and electrophysiology, we show that DHA accumulates around ASIC3 through interactions with a membrane-facing electropositive region along the outer leaflet of TM1. In the open state, a more buried binding site for the lipid is exposed that allows the carboxylate head group to bind a critical arginine along with nearby polar residues. Mutation of this site eliminates the DHA-mediated slowing of channel desensitization and also modestly reduces the effect PUFAs have on the proton sensitivity of channel activation. The same mutations do not prevent regulation by other lipid classes like N-acyl amino acids or lysophosphatidyl choline. Our results provide the first detailed description of a PUFA binding site on ASICs, offering new insights into lipid modulation and potential strategies for developing novel treatments for inflammatory pain.

papers.title: Flavonoid chronotherapy normalizes circadian dynamics and sleep architecture in mice with painful nerve injury
papers.abstract: Neuropathic pain (NP) is linked to disrupted sleep and circadian abnormalities upon painful peripheral nerve injury. By performing spared nerve injury (SNI) in circadian reporter PER2::LUC mice, we characterized the real-time changes in rhythmicity of the core clock gene Per2 in the pain-regulating dorsal root ganglia (DRG), and the sleep-wake cycle using wireless EEG/EMG under NP conditions. We further evaluated whether the clock-resynchronizing flavonoids, nobiletin (2 mg/kg/day) and tangeretin (1.8 mg/kg/day), administered continuously via osmotic minipumps for two weeks, could restore circadian dynamics and alleviate pain-related behaviour. Both flavonoids alleviated SNI-induced dynamic hypersensitivity in PER2::LUC mice on post-surgical day 14. SNI increased the amplitude of Per2 rhythms in the DRGs, which was restored to pre-surgical levels by administration of flavonoids. In addition, tangeretin showed sleep-restoring properties upon SNI by alleviating disturbances in NREM sleep and wakefulness. These results support targeting circadian disruption as a potential chronotherapeutic approach to alleviate NP.

papers.title: Longitudinal persistence of EEG brain fingerprints:phase and complex coherency geometry across sessions andfunctional states
papers.abstract: EEG connectivity can distinguish individuals, but the persistence of its phase and magnitude structure across visits and functional states remains incompletely understood. We examined two geometric representations of complex coherency: unit phasors and full complex coherency, alongside triangle holonomies and magnitude-only descriptors. Using direct enrollment-probe matching without a trained identity classifier, we analyzed three independent longitudinal cohorts: RestCog (N = 60; approximately one month), L-FAME (N = 44; six weeks), and Dortmund (N = 206; approximately five years). In eyes-closed rest-to-rest matching, alpha phasors identified 81.67% of participants in RestCog (AUC 0.9473) and 79.55% in L-FAME (AUC 0.9735); full complex coherency identified 78.33% and 84.09%, respectively. After five years in Dortmund, fixed row-standardized alpha-beta fusion yielded 77.67% rank-1 identification (AUC 0.9744) for phasors and 70.39% (AUC 0.9527) for full coherency. Changes in functional state exposed different strengths: full coherency preserved higher rank-1 accuracy in some monthly RestCog rest-to-task comparisons, whereas alpha phasors retained higher verification AUC. Switching between eyes-closed and eyes-open recordings in Dortmund substantially weakened identification with both representations. Triangle holonomies also retained individual information across visits. An exact factorization of complex cosine shows how magnitude-pattern alignment and magnitude-weighted phase agreement contribute to full-coherency matching. Together, the results reveal persistent individual structure in both phase and complex coherency over weeks to years, while distinguishing temporal persistence from robustness across functional states.

papers.title: Decoding and Characterizing the Intracranial Representation of Semantic Information
papers.abstract: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) have achieved impressive performance by decoding motor and articulatory signals associated with speech production. However, considerably less is known about whether higher-level semantic representations can be decoded from human cortical activity. Demonstrating semantic decoding would advance both our understanding of language organization and the development of BCIs that rely on conceptual rather than purely articulatory information. We recorded intracranial neural activity from patients undergoing stereotactic electroencephalography (sEEG) for clinical epilepsy monitoring while they performed language tasks requiring semantic processing. High-gamma power was extracted from local field potentials and used to generate trial-level features for supervised machine-learning classification. Classification performance was evaluated using cross-validation. Semantic category information was decoded significantly above chance, with mean classification accuracy reaching 29.8% across 15 semantic categories (chance = 6.7%). These findings demonstrate that high-gamma activity contains information about conceptual category membership that can be extracted on individual trials. These results provide evidence that semantic information is accessible from intracranial population recordings and support the feasibility of semantic decoding as a complementary direction for future language BCIs. Beyond neuroprosthetic applications, this work contributes to understanding how conceptual knowledge is represented in the distributed human language network.

papers.title: Ensemble viewing reshapes neural representations of same-race and other-race faces
papers.abstract: The other-race effect, better recognition of same-race than other-race faces, is established for individual faces. Whether this benefit is reflected in neural representations of face ensembles, as when viewing a crowd, remains unclear. We recorded electroencephalography responses from 22 East Asian adults viewing synthetic East Asian (same-race) and White (other-race) faces in two formats: individually and in six-face ensembles. Multivariate decoding and generative image reconstruction assessed neural discriminability, representational geometry and recoverable visual content. Behavioral testing confirmed a same-race recognition advantage. The corresponding neural decoding advantage depended on viewing format and was not preserved for race-homogeneous ensembles, although their constituents retained it when viewed individually. Early ensemble decoding instead favored other-race faces. Race organized ensemble representations and reconstructed latent vectors matched ensemble summary targets above chance. Independent judgments revealed format-dependent race differences in reconstructed age and arousal relative to model-derived references. These findings constrain accounts of same-race expertise: its benefit for neural discriminability depends on whether faces are represented individually or collectively. Recoverable ensemble-summary information can also coexist with systematic appearance shifts, linking the organization of neural representations to their visual content.

papers.title: Tetradic Dynamics of Dyadic Sensorimotor Coordination: A Multiscale EEG Hyperscanning Study
papers.abstract: How do leader and follower roles shape the brain mechanisms that support coordinated action between people? This question has therapeutic relevance for conditions such as schizophrenia and autism spectrum disorder, where the capacity for reciprocal social coordination is a defining vulnerability. Here, we propose a tetradic framework and examine sensorimotor coordination in 16 healthy adult pairs (15 included in EEG analyses) using dual-brain EEG hyperscanning and a 2x2 within-subject design crossing Role (Leader/Follower) and Condition (Mirroring/Matching). Mirroring required resonance with a partner's movement; Matching required its controlled transformation. This contrast was designed to dissociate automatic from controlled coordination. Behaviourally, Mirroring produced a robust Follower reaction-time advantage: pooling an independent behavioural-only cohort (combined N=64) revealed a smaller Leader advantage, consistent with role-dependent attention-inhibition gating. At the neural level, tonic power and significant phasic condition clusters were greater during Matching than Mirroring, while role-dependent phasic clusters suggested an anticipatory sequence around Leader responses and post-response gating and rebound around Follower responses. Information-theoretic decomposition identified Leader-unique predictive information in superior temporal regions and a separate frontal-pole interaction, Follower-unique predictive information in insular and superior frontal regions, sparse Synergy in the right rostral anterior cingulate cortex, and Redundancy spanning multiple cortical regions. These findings characterize tetradic coordination within dyads as a multiscale, role-asymmetric architecture in which top-down predictive control and bottom-up adaptive regulation are functionally dissociable. The tetradic framework provides a scaffold for this dissociation, and the role-specific signatures it reveals may offer candidate biomarkers for clinical populations in whom interpersonal coordination is disrupted.

papers.title: A multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset with repeated experience sampling
papers.abstract: The integration of electroencephalography (EEG) and functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) can be used to characterize temporal and spatial components of neural activity during unfolding mental experience. Here we introduce a multi-session simultaneous EEG-fMRI dataset with measures of continuous behavior and spontaneous mental experience. Data components, organized in Brain Imaging Dataset Structure (BIDS) format, include fMRI, EEG with carbon wire loop sensors for artifact removal, continuous performance task responses, experience sampling ratings, and mental health surveys, from 24 healthy adults. Tasks included the gradual-onset continuous performance task and resting state with intermittent experience sampling of 13 unique thought dimensions (36 repetitions, including 468 total ratings, per participant). The same protocol was completed on two different days, yielding approximately 1.33 hours of simultaneous EEG-fMRI data per individual. The dataset may be used to explore the behavioral and experiential relevance of brain activity during the wakeful resting state. The dataset also provides a means to study the reliability of relationships between fMRI and EEG features across sessions within individuals.
